newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican metal workers' unions protest pay offer.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican metal workers' unions protest pay offer.

text.p: Metal and engineering industry unions on Wednesday rejected an offer by employers to raise the industry's minimum wage by 52 cents per hour arguing for more pay increases, an employers' body said.

The Steel and Engineering Industries Federation of South Africa (SEIFSA) said the workers had stood by their demand for a wage hike ranging from 18 to 21.4 percent during a second round of annual wage talks.

"Representatives of the industry's party trade unions rejected the employers' wage offer and argued the need for a greater wage increase. The unions did not modify their wage demands which range from 18 to 21.4 percent," a SEIFSA statement said.
The employers offer sought to raise the industry's minimum wage to 7.92 rand an hour, approximately 1,509 rand a month, the statement added.
It said employers and the unions had undertaken to reconsider their respective positions ahead of a final round of wage talks scheduled to take place on June 12 and 13.
